title: Extracted Claim
description: One reusable building block of the tafsir knowledge layer: a single claim or observation drawn from fetched commentary, kept in a consistent, source-traceable shape so it can power the Overview essay today and future projects (audio, comparison, research export) later. Distinct from the final rendered essay.

attaches_to.description: Verse or verse:word the claim is about, e.g. '87:3' or '87:3:2'. Preserves sub-section attachment.

text.description: The claim, in English, as what the source says — not independent interpretation.

basis.description: How the claim is derived — lets rhetoric-argued readings stay distinct from report-based ones.

sources.description: The fetched commentary/commentaries behind this claim. More than one source is NOT independent corroboration unless the authors are chronologically/traditionally independent (see commentators.json).

author_id.description: Matches an author id in commentators.json (for chronology / dependency checks).

stance.description: Whether the citing commentator endorses, neutrally relays, or refutes the point.

source_language.description: Language of the underlying work (ISO code), e.g. 'ar', 'ur', 'bn'.

original_excerpt.description: Optional verbatim source text in its own language.

english_rendering.description: Optional model translation into English (rendering, not a verbatim quote).

original_terms.description: Technical terms preserved with a plain gloss, so the original is always recoverable.

report.description: Present only when the claim rests on a narration (hadith/athar).

graded_by.description: Who assigns the grade, or the source that leaves it ungraded.

theological_school.description: e.g. 'Ashʿarī', 'Māturīdī', 'Atharī', 'Muʿtazilī' — set when the reading is creedally committed.

provenance.description: How this claim was produced — needed for reproducibility and drift-auditing.

source_hash.description: Hash of the raw fetched text this claim was extracted from.
